images.caption: Preserved East Yorkshire 747, a Park Royal 'Beverley Bar'-bodied AEC Bridgemaster repainted back into period National Bus Company livery, passing under Beverley Bar for the second time on its post-repaint debut in August 2022. 747 is the first double-decker to pass under the Bar since the 1980s, and like all East Yorkshire buses prior to the early 70s, is built with a roof specifically curved inwards to navigate the Bar.

images.caption: North Bar, Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.Participants in the Walkington Hayride pass through the North Bar gate on their way into Beverley town centre. The charity event was founded by Ernie Teal in 1967 but this is expected to be the last procession due to dwindling numbers of heavy horses and horsemen. North Bar (the brick arch in the centre of the picture) is the only one remaining of a number of gates which once guarded the entrances to Beverley. It was built by the town council in 1409 and cost a fraction over £96.

images.caption:
Junction of North Bar Without and Wylies and York Roads, Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.
Two laides on horseback turn left out of North Bar Without into Wylies Road; if they had turned right they would have entered York Road. Ahead of us, through 1295818, North Bar Without becomes North Bar Within.

images.caption: North Bar Within, Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.The North Bar is the sole surviving bar, or gate, of the four that were built in the Middle Ages to control the main route entries into Beverley. The area of the town on this side of the bar is known as "within", the other side is known as "without", i.e. outside the gate. The present gate was rebuilt in 1409 from bricks that had been made locally in Beverley.
images.alt: North Bar Within, Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.The North Bar is the sole surviving bar, or gate, of the four that were built in the Middle Ages to control the main route entries into Beverley. The area of the town on this side of the bar is known as "within", the other side is known as "without", i.e. outside the gate. The present gate was rebuilt in 1409 from bricks that had been made locally in Beverley.

images.caption:
North Bar, Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire, England.This medieval gateway was rebuilt in brick in 1409/10 AD.
The North Bar, is the oldest surviving brick built bar in England and is the only remaining town gate of four which guarded the towns main entrances during medieval times.
